sections.h2: Which Troy offices bill, collect and value property?
sections.html:
Troy's summer and winter bills come from the City Treasurer's Office in City Hall at 500 W Big Beaver Road, which keeps weekday hours of 8 to 4:30. Oakland County surrounds the city, and its treasurer picks up whatever Troy has not collected by March 1.

One Troy bill funds many bodies. Besides city services, the city collects and passes along tax for seven school districts, the county, the Huron-Clinton Metropolitan Authority, the county's art, zoo and transit authorities, Oakland Schools and the Macomb Intermediate School District. A house's school district shapes the millage, and the city posts a Millage Rates page for that reason.

The City Assessor's Office covers values. It appraises each parcel, processes splits and combinations, and runs the Principal Residence Exemption and Property Transfer Affidavit programs. Call it at 248-524-3311.

sections.h2: What are the Troy tax due dates and late charges?
sections.html:
Summer statements are mailed July 1 and payable through September 1. Winter statements are mailed December 1 and payable through February 14. A deadline that falls on a weekend or city holiday slides forward one business day, as with the 2026 winter bills, which run through February 16, 2027.

  • Summer: 4% is added the first business day after September 1, and monthly interest of one-half of 1% begins October 1.
  • Winter: 3% is added the first business day after February 14.
  • March 1: anything unpaid for the current year is sent to Oakland County as delinquent, with fees and interest on top. The 2025 taxes turned delinquent on March 3, 2026.
  • A bill that never arrived is no excuse, and penalty and interest still apply.

After that point, payment goes to the Oakland County Treasurer in Pontiac at 248.858.0611, option 7. Ask for the current amount owing, because fees keep building.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Troy tax bill?
sections.html:
Troy accepts automatic debit, mail, cards, e-checks, bank bill pay and walk-in payment. A check or money order placed in an official drop box before 8 a.m. on the business day following a due date still counts as on time.

  • Automatic debit from checking or savings costs nothing, and for winter you choose February 14 or the last business day of December.
  • Cards cost 3%, with a floor of $1.50 online and $2.00 at the counter. E-checks are free below $10,000 and $10 from $10,000 up.
  • Red and blue Official Drop Boxes stand outside City Hall's east walk-up and west drive-up doors, for checks and money orders only.
  • Walk in with the entire statement. Cash, checks, money orders and cards are all taken.

The city's BS&A lookup prints bills and shows payments once you register, which costs nothing. The city calls a cleared check the best receipt, and it will mail a paper one if you supply a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

sections.h2: Is there help for Troy owners who cannot pay on time?
sections.html:
Yes, for qualifying households. A Property Tax Deferment moves the due date on both bills to the following April 30. Household income has to be $40,000 or less, and the owner must be 62 or older, paraplegic, hemiplegic or quadriplegic, totally and permanently disabled or blind, or an eligible service person, veteran, widow or widower.

Apply on Michigan Treasury Form 471, delivered to the Treasurer's Office by September 15 with last year's Homestead Property Tax Credit form attached. Questions go to 248.524.3333. Owners outside those groups avoid the March 1 transfer only by paying the winter bill in full on time.

sections.h2: What does the 2026 Troy assessment roll show?
sections.html:
Troy's 2026 roll holds 35,732 parcels with assessed value of $10,026,428,690 and taxable value of $7,270,919,530. Those totals are up 5.76% and 4.47% on 2025. The assessor's page says the combined state equalized value is projected above $10 billion.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Troy assessment or prepare for a reappraisal visit?
sections.html:
For a Troy homeowner, the March Board of Review is the single chance to contest a residential value, and a missed session means waiting a year. Mid-February brings a notice of assessment to every property whose assessed value changed, listing protest dates. If it never reaches you, the values still stand.

When city appraisers visit, they carry marked badges and measure the outside of the house and any improvements. Participation is voluntary, and staff do not need to enter the home, although they ask about the interior and mail a survey. General maintenance such as new gutters, a roof or windows is not assessable. What raises value is air conditioning, decks, porches, patios, sheds, additions, garages, finished basements and added bathrooms. Appointments run through the Assessing Department, with field slots between 9:00 a.m. and 2:30 p.m.

The department processed about 2,448 recorded deeds in 2025, and most produced a Property Transfer Affidavit. It handles a similar number of Principal Residence Exemption affidavits each year. Businesses must file personal property statements by February 20.

sections.h2: What is Troy like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Land sales in what became Troy began in 1819, and the township formed in 1827. Incorporation as a city came in 1955, partly to stop neighboring cities from annexing land. Troy covers about 33.5 square miles. Business here leans toward the automotive and financial sectors, and Somerset Collection and Oakland Mall anchor retail. Interstate 75 runs through, and Amtrak's Wolverine train stops at the Troy Transit Center beside Oakland-Troy Airport.

Seven districts reach into Troy. Troy School District serves most addresses, with Troy High School and Athens High School as its two zoned high schools. Avondale, Birmingham and Warren Consolidated also run schools inside the city, so confirm the district for any address you are marketing.

The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 88,733 residents. In the 2020 to 2024 survey, nearly three of four homes (73.3%) were owner-occupied at a median value of $420,300, and 64.8% of adults had a bachelor's degree or more. Median household income reached $120,045. Recent sales on the seller's own street will say more than any citywide median.

faqs.q: What is the penalty if I pay my Troy summer bill late?
faqs.a: A 4% penalty is added on the first business day after September 1, and one-half of 1% monthly interest starts October 1. The winter bill carries a 3% penalty after February 14.

faqs.q: When does my Troy tax bill go to Oakland County?
faqs.a: On March 1, every unpaid current-year bill is transferred to the Oakland County Treasurer as delinquent, with added fees and interest. Pay the county at 1200 N Telegraph Rd, Dept 479, Pontiac, or call 248.858.0611, option 7.

faqs.q: Can I deduct a Troy payment from my bank automatically?
faqs.a: Yes, at no fee. Troy withdraws the payment on the due date, and a separate enrollment form is needed for property tax and for water and sewer. For the winter bill you choose February 14 or the last business day in December.

faqs.q: Who do I call in Troy about my home's value?
faqs.a: Call the Assessing Department at 248-524-3311. Office hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and appraiser visits can be booked for slots between 9:00 a.m. and 2:30 p.m.

faqs.q: How much time do Troy owners have to appeal a residential value?
faqs.a: The only window is the March Board of Review, and it applies to the current year. If you miss it, you give up the right to appeal that year's value.
